questions.prompt: One dog, two ___
questions.explanation: Most words just add -s to make more than one: dog, dogs.
questions.audioText: One dog, two blank. Which word fits?

questions.prompt: One box, two ___
questions.explanation: Box ends in x, so we add -es: boxes.
questions.audioText: One box, two blank. Which word fits?

questions.prompt: One brush, two ___
questions.explanation: Brush ends in sh, so we add -es: brushes.
questions.audioText: One brush, two blank. Which word fits?

questions.prompt: Tick the two words that add -es to make more than one.
questions.explanation: Fox ends in x and bus ends in s, so they become foxes and buses. Cat and hat just add -s.

questions.prompt: Which word means not happy?
questions.explanation: Un- goes at the start and means not: unhappy.

questions.prompt: Sam had to ___ his coat to take it off.
questions.explanation: Unzip means the opposite of zip.
questions.audioText: Sam had to blank his coat to take it off. Which word fits?

questions.prompt: The door was not locked. It was ___.
questions.explanation: Not locked is unlocked.
questions.audioText: The door was not locked. It was blank.

questions.prompt: Yesterday I ___ over the puddle.
questions.explanation: Yesterday is in the past, so we add -ed: jumped.
questions.audioText: Yesterday I blank over the puddle.

questions.prompt: Look! The bird is ___.
questions.explanation: Is goes with -ing to show it is happening now: is singing.

questions.prompt: A person who helps is a ___.
questions.explanation: Adding -er can mean a person who does something: help, helper.

questions.prompt: Add -ing to the word play.
questions.explanation: Play plus -ing is playing. Nothing else changes.
questions.audioText: Add i n g to play. Spell playing.

questions.prompt: I like apples ___ I like pears.
questions.explanation: And joins two ideas together.
questions.audioText: I like apples blank I like pears.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses and to join two ideas?
questions.explanation: And joins I ran with I jumped to make one sentence.

questions.prompt: Join these with and: I have a cat. I have a dog.
answers: I have a cat and I have a dog.
I have a cat and a dog.
questions.explanation: Take away the first full stop and join the two ideas with and: I have a cat and I have a dog.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is written correctly?
questions.explanation: A sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.

questions.prompt: Write it again with a capital letter and a full stop: we went to the park
questions.explanation: Start with a capital W and finish with a full stop: We went to the park.

questions.prompt: Tap where the full stop should go.
questions.explanation: The first sentence ends after down: The cat sat down. It went to sleep.
questions.audioText: The cat sat down it went to sleep. Tap where the full stop should go.

questions.prompt: Which mark goes at the end? Where is my hat
questions.explanation: Where is my hat is asking something, so it needs a question mark.

questions.prompt: Which mark goes at the end? Ouch, that hurt
questions.explanation: Ouch shows a strong feeling, so it needs an exclamation mark.

questions.prompt: Tick the two questions.
questions.explanation: Questions ask something and end with a question mark.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is written correctly?
choices: Mia and I went to London.
mia and i went to london.
Mia and i went to London.
mia and I went to london.
answers: Mia and I went to London.
questions.explanation: Names of people and places start with a capital letter, and I is always a capital.

questions.prompt: Tick the two words that always need a capital letter.
questions.explanation: Days of the week and names of places always start with a capital letter.

questions.prompt: Write it again with the right capital letters: on friday i saw ben.
questions.explanation: On starts the sentence, Friday is a day, I is always a capital and Ben is a name.
